title: uvSphere
body:
## uvSphere

Creates a closed sphere mesh with Blender's bmesh UV-sphere generator: segments meridians around the local Z axis and rings latitude bands between the poles, all vertices on the given radius about centre. Faces crowd towards the poles; choose icoSphere for evenly sized triangles, for example before voxelRemesh or wireframe.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The mesh is inscribed in the true sphere, so its volume is below 4/3 pi r cubed; raise segments and rings when volume or silhouette accuracy matters.
- The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

Native binding: `uvSphere`. Output kind: `["data"]`.

| Input port | Multiplicity | Required | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `material` | one node | yes | `material` |

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `radius` | Radius of the sphere on which all vertices lie. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"exclusiveMinimum":true}` | `1` |
| `segments` | Number of meridians around the local Z axis (longitude divisions). Raise it together with rings for smoother silhouettes; about twice rings gives roughly square faces at the equator. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":3,"maximum":256}` | `32` |
| `rings` | Number of latitude bands from pole to pole (the generator's v segments). More rings smooth the profile seen from the side. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":3,"maximum":256}` | `16` |
| `centre` | World position [x, y, z] of the sphere's centre. Schemaxis assigns it as the object's location, so the mesh itself stays about the local origin and later modifiers that work about that origin (mirror, bend, twist) use this point. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[0,0,0]` |
| `smoothShading` | When true, every face of the generated uvSphere is marked smooth so Blender interpolates normals and the tessellated surface renders without visible facets; when false the faces render flat. Geometry and vertex positions are identical either way. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `false` |
